problem: Navigation world models pick their frozen visual state space mostly by reconstruction quality, and use Global-Softmax history attention that recomputes the same history for every candidate action, so cost and memory blow up with long histories and many planning queries.
motivation: A representation that reconstructs well need not be predictable under actions, and autoregressive rollout accumulates errors, so reconstruction, direct prediction and rollout may favor different representations. Planning evaluates many candidate actions on one shared history, so reusable history computation is needed for long-context, multi-query prediction.
key_idea: Benchmark five frozen visual representations under one conditional flow-transformer NWM, and add reusable-history mixers (Cached-Linear and Balanced GDN with frame-wise recurrent memory) that amortize history computation across candidate queries.
insight: No single representation wins: PAE-L is best at reconstruction (0.069 DINO), RAE-B at direct prediction, V-JEPA at long rollout (overtakes RAE-B after 3.25 s). History mixers give near-identical Avg-4 DINO (0.5300 / 0.5310 / 0.5314) but very different cost: at 64 frames and 120 queries Cached-Linear cuts latency from 51.67 s to 7.15 s. Image-metric gains do not transfer to open-loop trajectory error, where RAE/Softmax wins all columns, and adding iREPA hurt DINO in all 12 comparisons.
method: Conditional flow-matching NWM: frozen encoder gives a 16x16 latent grid; a 12-block CDiT-B/2 (width 768) with a 2-block DDT head predicts velocity, conditioned on history, action (dx,dy,dtheta), horizon and flow time; Euler-50 sampling and a frozen decoder.

Frozen representation benchmark: RAE-B, RAE-L (DINOv2 dense), PAE-L (32-channel compact), Cosmos-CI16, V-JEPA 2.1 with S-VAE adapter. Compared by decoded-image metrics, with the reconstruction reference kept separate from end-to-end prediction.

Cached-Linear: target self-attention uses 8x8 window attention plus shifted-window attention. History is compressed once into an ELU+1 kernelized summary (M,u) that every query reads, so history cost is not repeated per candidate.

Balanced GDN: replaces one self-mixing block per 4-block group with a frame-wise Gated Delta Network (recurrent state S, normalizer r, token-wise write gate, per-frame retention gate). Schedule per group: self (GDN,W,W,A_j), cross (L,L,L,SWA), with a final full-attention anchor block.
Auxiliary iREPA: a 3x3 conv aligns one intermediate dynamics feature to the clean visual feature, used only in training and removed at inference.

Inference modes and diagnostics: direct prediction from real history vs autoregressive rollout that feeds predicted latents back without decode/re-encode; conditioning-corruption tests and a linear SE(2) motion probe; open-loop CEM-120 trajectory prediction.

setting.backbone: CDiT-B/2 flow transformer (about 350M params) on frozen RAE/PAE/Cosmos/V-JEPA encoders and decoders, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: RECON, SACSoN, SCAND; 62,813 observations per dataset per epoch, 4 future targets each; 10 epochs (Study I, ablation) or 50 epochs (main experiment)
setting.observation: monocular RGB history (8 frames by default; up to 128 in systems tests), encoded to 16x16 latent grids
setting.action_space: relative planar displacement (dx, dy, dtheta) with a requested time horizon; open-loop CEM-120 trajectory prediction
setting.simulator: none (offline real-robot datasets RECON, SACSoN, SCAND)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark (R2R, ObjectNav etc.) is used. Numbers are for a world-model prediction task on RECON/SACSoN/SCAND, so the benchmark is given as other:. Split labelled 'test' as held-out trajectories. Many further tables (Study I, ablation matrix, 10-epoch runs, systems efficiency) exist but only the main-experiment rows are listed.
results: Study I shows the best representation changes with the objective: PAE-L for reconstruction (0.069), RAE-B for direct prediction (0.574/0.608 DINO at Direct@16/32), V-JEPA for rollout (0.761/0.771). The three history mixers have near-identical Avg-4 DINO, while Cached-Linear cuts 64-frame, 120-query latency from 51.67 s to 7.15 s and memory from 34.63 GiB to 5.35 GiB, and Global-Softmax runs out of memory at 128 frames. Balanced GDN improves RAE-B Direct@32 (0.554 to 0.540), but RAE/Global-Softmax gives the best open-loop trajectory ATE/RPE on all three datasets.
limitations: Single training seed and open-loop evaluation only, with no closed-loop navigation; Balanced GDN does not improve rollout stability or trajectory error.
Kernelized linear attention drops some pairwise interactions, and quality gains are inconsistent across representations, metrics and datasets; iREPA gave no benefit.
The frozen features contain no linear encoding of relative motion (negative R²), and the 3x4 component study was exploratory with shorter training (10 epochs).
